parts.name: Left Button
parts.Basic_description: This is the left button of a computer mouse made of ABS plastic, typically located on the top-left side of the mouse.
parts.Functional_description: It is used for primary clicking actions such as selecting, dragging, and interacting with software interfaces.
parts.Movement_description: It moves vertically downward when pressed and returns to its original position via a spring mechanism.

parts.name: Right Button
parts.Basic_description: This is the right button of a computer mouse made of ABS plastic, positioned on the top-right side.
parts.Functional_description: It is used for secondary clicking actions such as opening context menus or performing alternate functions.
parts.Movement_description: It moves vertically downward when pressed and returns to its original position via a spring mechanism.

parts.name: Scroll Wheel
parts.Basic_description: This is the scroll wheel of the mouse, typically made of rubber for better grip and tactile feedback.
parts.Functional_description: It allows the user to scroll vertically or horizontally through content and can also act as a middle button when pressed.
parts.Movement_description: It rotates around its horizontal axis and can also be pressed downward for additional input.

parts.name: Base Body
parts.Basic_description: This is the main body or shell of the mouse, made of durable ABS plastic, providing structure and housing for internal components.
parts.Functional_description: It supports all other parts, provides ergonomic shape for hand placement, and houses electronic components such as sensors and circuit boards.
parts.Movement_description: It remains stationary relative to the internal components but moves as a whole when the user moves the mouse across a surface.
